name: Focus-preserving asynchronous button feedback
summary: One documented implementation represents in-progress action state with a spinner, aria-disabled, accessible status text and retained label/focus structure.
problem: Async actions can leave users unsure whether an operation is still in progress, while remounts or unconditional native disabling may disrupt focus.
context: A control starts an asynchronous operation and should not trigger the same action twice while progress is pending.
observed_solution: Primer documents loading with a spinner and focus retention; pinned ButtonBase code retains a wrapper, sets aria-disabled, suppresses its click handler, and emits an AriaStatus announcement.
rationale: Documentation (W02-O13) and pinned source inspection (W02-O17) support the presence of that implementation strategy; WCAG name/role/state and status-message criteria bound the accessibility goal without proving actual conformance.
tradeoffs: ARIA disabled alone does not enforce every possible activation path; consumer integration matters.
Live announcements may be repeated or missed depending on caller/browser/assistive technology and must be tested.
A forced loading state with no recovery may cause a different usability failure.
applicability: Button-triggered asynchronous actions where repeat activation should pause and focus continuity matters.
non_applicability: Navigation links for which progress is represented at the destination.
Actions that complete instantly or require a different interaction feedback model.
accessibility_implications: Inspect name/role/state and status announcement in context; code inspection is not WCAG conformance evidence.
performance_implications: No performance measurements; spinner/rendering implementation costs unknown.
responsive_implications: Not evaluated at mobile or reduced-motion settings.
implementation_notes: Do not universalize one React implementation or claim tests were executed.

counterexamples.summary: GOV.UK discusses disabled submission buttons without claiming this loading structure.
counterexamples.context: Static state where action cannot be taken and no async operation is underway.
